findings.title: Shared preloaded SSLContext gets per-request client certs loaded into it
findings.suggested_fix: Only use the shared preloaded context when client_cert is None; when a client cert is supplied, omit ssl_context and fall back to ca_certs=DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH (extract_zipped_paths) so urllib3 builds a private context. Alternatively hand each pool a copy (e.g. a cached context per cert) instead of the single module-level object. Assumption: cert+verify=True is less common than plain verify=True, so the slow path there is acceptable.

findings.title: Preloaded context overrides ssl_context set in HTTPAdapter subclasses
findings.suggested_fix: In _urllib3_request_context (or in _get_connection, which has the adapter), set pool_kwargs['ssl_context'] = _preloaded_ssl_context only if the target manager's connection_pool_kw has no 'ssl_context' already, e.g. check self.poolmanager.connection_pool_kw / proxy manager kwargs. Assumption: adapter-provided ssl_context should win over the built-in default.

residual_risks: Import-time side effect: _preloaded_ssl_context is built at module import via load_verify_locations(extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)). A missing or unreadable certifi bundle now makes `import requests` raise, instead of the previous per-request OSError('Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle'). cert_verify no longer performs that existence check for verify=True. This contradicts the stated goal of preserving missing-bundle errors and adds import cost, but I could not confirm a realistic environment where the bundle is absent.

The shared context is process-wide and mutated by urllib3 per connection (verify_mode, check_hostname when assert_hostname or pyOpenSSL is used, set_alpn_protocols); concurrent use across sessions and adapters with differing pool kwargs relies on those mutations being idempotent.
testing_gaps: No test covers verify=True combined with a client cert (cert=...) asserting the shared context is not mutated, nor an HTTPAdapter subclass supplying its own ssl_context with verify=True.

findings.title: Shared module-level SSLContext leaks client certificates across requests (CWE-200, CWE-501)
findings.suggested_fix: In _urllib3_request_context, only set pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context when verify is True AND client_cert is None. When client_cert is set with verify=True, keep the previous per-connection path (no ssl_context; set ca_certs to the default bundle path, or build a per-cert-key context cache: copy of the preloaded context via create_urllib3_context + load_verify_locations once, keyed by (cert_file, key_file)). Add a regression test that a request with cert= followed by one without does not present the client cert.

findings.title: verify=True silently overrides adapter-configured ssl_context, dropping custom TLS policy (CWE-295)
findings.suggested_fix: Only set pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context if the adapter's poolmanager.connection_pool_kw has no "ssl_context" (thread the adapter/poolmanager into _urllib3_request_context, or use pool_kwargs.setdefault semantics by checking self.poolmanager.connection_pool_kw). Add a test using an adapter whose init_poolmanager supplies ssl_context.

residual_risks: Shared context is also mutated by urllib3 per connection (verify_mode, check_hostname=False when assert_hostname/fingerprint/pyOpenSSL is used, set_alpn_protocols); a custom adapter passing assert_hostname=False would flip check_hostname on the process-wide context for all verify=True traffic (urllib3 falls back to its own hostname match for other connections, so verification is preserved, but the shared state is fragile).
testing_gaps: No test asserts that a request using cert= does not leave the client certificate loaded in the shared context seen by later verify=True requests.
No test covers an HTTPAdapter subclass supplying its own ssl_context together with the default verify=True.

findings.title: Shared global SSLContext accumulates client certs, leaking one session's identity to others
findings.suggested_fix: In _urllib3_request_context, only set pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context when client_cert is None; when client_cert is set with verify=True, fall back to the previous behavior (ca_certs = default bundle path, no shared context) so the client cert is loaded into a per-connection context. Add a test that a second cert-less request after a cert= request does not present the client cert.
findings.first_evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:75 -- _preloaded_ssl_context = create_urllib3_context()  (module-level, shared by all pools); adapters.py:95 -- pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context; adapters.py:104-109 -- pool_kwargs["cert_file"] / ["key_file"] still set independently of ssl_context

findings.title: verify=True pool_kwargs ssl_context silently replaces adapter's custom SSLContext
findings.suggested_fix: In _get_connection (or _urllib3_request_context via a passed-in adapter poolmanager), skip pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] when self.poolmanager.connection_pool_kw already contains an ssl_context (and likewise for proxy_manager), falling back to ca_certs/default behavior so user contexts are respected.

residual_risks: Import-time side effect: requests.adapters now builds an SSLContext and calls load_verify_locations(extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)) at import. A missing/unreadable certifi bundle (stripped or relocated certifi, zipapp extraction failure) now raises at `import requests` instead of the old request-time OSError, and the bundle is frozen at import so later changes to DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH/certifi or CA rotation in long-running processes are ignored. Adds import latency for users who never make an HTTPS request.

Other per-connection mutations of the shared context by urllib3 (context.verify_mode, context.check_hostname = False when assert_hostname=False/fingerprint/pyOpenSSL) now leak process-wide across adapters; hostname is still re-checked manually by urllib3 for other pools so this looks like reduced context-level defense rather than a bypass, but I did not exhaustively verify concurrency interleavings.

cert_verify no longer sets conn.ca_certs/ca_cert_dir for verify=True, so third-party subclasses or code that inspect/override conn.ca_certs after cert_verify(), or that mutate pool ca_certs on a verify=True pool, will silently see None/have no effect because the shared context is used.
testing_gaps: No test asserts that a request with cert=(...) does not contaminate later cert-less verify=True requests (shared context isolation), nor that an adapter-supplied ssl_context via init_poolmanager is honored when verify=True.

findings.title: Shared preloaded SSLContext mutated by client cert; no isolation test
findings.suggested_fix: Add a regression test: make a verify=True + cert=(client.pem, client.key) request that fails, then assert _preloaded_ssl_context.cert_store_stats() / a subsequent handshake to a mTLS server with no cert does not present a client cert (or assert the context object passed to urllib3 is not the shared one when client_cert is set). Fix in code by only passing the shared context when client_cert is None (otherwise fall back to ca_certs/default path), or by copying the context per client-cert pool.

findings.title: No test that verify=True routes the preloaded context or leaves ca_certs unset
findings.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized unit test on adapters._urllib3_request_context over verify in {True, False, None?, file path, directory path} asserting pool_kwargs: True -> pool_kwargs['ssl_context'] is adapters._preloaded_ssl_context and no ca_certs/ca_cert_dir; False -> cert_reqs CERT_NONE and no ssl_context; file -> ca_certs; dir (tmp_path) -> ca_cert_dir. Add an HTTPAdapter.cert_verify test with a stub conn asserting verify=True sets cert_reqs='CERT_REQUIRED' and does not set ca_certs/ca_cert_dir, and str file/dir set the right attribute.

findings.title: New directory-verify branch untested end to end
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the TLSServer-based bundle tests (tests/test_requests.py near line 2897) with a variant using verify=<tmp dir containing hashed copy of tests/certs/valid/ca/ca.crt> (or at least a unit assertion that pool_kwargs has ca_cert_dir and no ca_certs for a tmp_path directory).

residual_risks: Positive verify=True path (valid public/CA-signed cert accepted using the preloaded certifi context) is not covered offline; a test would need to patch adapters._preloaded_ssl_context to trust tests/certs/valid/ca/ca.crt, which is not done today.
test_pyopenssl_redirect and test_different_connection_pool_for_tls_settings_verify_bundle_unexpired_cert fail at base as stated; they cannot serve as regression signal for this change.
Behavior when the module-level _preloaded_ssl_context creation fails at import (e.g. missing certifi bundle) is untested; not run in this review.
testing_gaps: No test for HTTPAdapter.cert_verify(conn, https_url, True, None): conn.cert_reqs == 'CERT_REQUIRED' with ca_certs/ca_cert_dir untouched (contract change for subclassers of cert_verify).
No test that verify=False after verify=True on the same session does not inherit ssl_context / uses a distinct pool (only pool counts for verify=False vs True are asserted, not pool_kwargs).

findings.title: Shared ssl_context overrides adapter's custom ssl_context/ssl_version for verify=True
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the pool/proxy manager into _urllib3_request_context and set pool_kwargs['ssl_context'] = _preloaded_ssl_context only when verify is True and 'ssl_context' not in manager.connection_pool_kw (assumption: also skip when the subclass set ssl_version). Add a regression test with an HTTPAdapter subclass whose init_poolmanager passes ssl_context=<custom> and assert the connection pool uses it.

findings.title: Client cert= is loaded into the process-wide shared SSLContext
findings.suggested_fix: Do not inject the shared context when client_cert is not None (fall back to the pre-change path with ca_certs, or build a per-pool copy of the context that loads the default bundle plus the client cert). Add a test that a cert= request does not mutate _preloaded_ssl_context.

findings.title: Missing CA bundle now breaks `import requests` and ignores later bundle-path overrides
findings.suggested_fix: Build the preloaded context lazily on first verify=True use (functools.lru_cache on a helper) and keep the existing 'Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle' OSError when the bundle is missing, so import stays side-effect-light and the error surface is unchanged.

residual_risks: cert_verify() is a documented subclass extension point; for verify=True it no longer sets conn.ca_certs / conn.ca_cert_dir (only cert_reqs), and its docstring still describes the old contract. Third-party overrides that call super() and then read or rely on conn.ca_certs (e.g. to inspect or wrap the bundle) now see None. No in-repo callers or tests depend on it (only adapters.py:536 calls it); external impact is inferred, not evidenced.

The shared preloaded context also mutates on each connection (urllib3 sets verify_mode and hostname-check state on a caller-supplied context); concurrent verify=True/assert_hostname variations could race on the singleton. Not exercised.
testing_gaps: No test covers an HTTPAdapter subclass supplying its own ssl_context via init_poolmanager with verify=True, or cert= not mutating the shared context; both would have caught the findings above.
